title: Company Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Subject to the insider trading rules, the prior written Chairman approval requirement, the 30-day short-term trading ban and the closed period ban; additionally must report any change in their securities holdings to the register within one business day.

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: Company employees. Subject to the same insider trading rules, prior written Chairman approval requirement, 30-day short-term trading ban and closed period ban as Directors; no separate holdings register obligation.

tiers.name: consultants
tiers.description: Consultants and contractors to the Company. Expressly covered by the insider trading policy, the prior approval requirement and the short-term trading ban; covered by the closed period ban only if the Company advises them that the provision applies to them.

tiers.name: Person
tiers.description: The label used in the closed periods section: the Company's directors, employees and such of the Company's contractors as the Company shall advise are covered by that provision. This is the group barred from trading in securities or derivatives during closed periods and the group able to apply for an exceptional circumstances exemption.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman is the approver for everyone else; where an obligation under the policy applies to the Chairman himself, the approval or notification is made to the Managing Director instead.

windows.start_anchor: 2 business days prior to the announcement by the Company of its quarterly, half-year or full year results
windows.end_anchor: the date and time of the announcement of those results (the Announcement Date)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to declare additional blackout periods. However the Chairman may refuse clearance for any proposed trade if he believes the Company is in possession of inside information or that the proposed trade is 'for any other reason, not in the best interests of the Company', which operates as an unbounded discretionary block at any time; the policy does not say whether reasons are given or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives are named only once, in the closed period ban, where trading in 'any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities' is prohibited during a closed period. There is no venue limitation, so exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls are both caught. Outside closed periods there is no express derivatives prohibition; a derivative transaction over Company securities is a proposed transaction in the Company's securities requiring prior written advice to, and written permission from, the Chairman.
rules.evidence: it is prohibited, under this policy, that the Company's directors, employees and such of the Company's contractors that the Company shall advise are covered by this provision ("Person") trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The policy contains no hedging provision at all: it does not define hedging, does not refer to limiting economic risk, and draws no distinction between vested and unvested securities or between plan and non-plan securities. Nothing in the document prohibits hedging of Company securities as such; a hedge would be regulated only as a trade or derivative under the clearance and closed period rules.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A monetisation of Company securities is a proposed transaction in the Company's securities and so requires prior written notice to the Chairman and written confirmation that it is permissible; if structured as a derivative it is also caught by the closed period ban. There is no prohibition on monetisation as such.
rules.evidence: it is a requirement that any employee, consultant or Director proposing to trade in Company securities first advise the Chairman (in writing) of the details of such proposed trade and not trade until the Chairman advise that such trade is permissible.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no dealing definition that would sweep it in.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities is a derivative created over or in respect of the Company's securities and so is banned during closed periods and otherwise requires prior written Chairman approval as a proposed trade. A CFD opened and closed within 30 days would also breach the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin loans and margin accounts are not mentioned anywhere in the policy, and there is no provision dealing with forced sales by a lender or with margin calls falling in a closed period.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, and there is no definition of dealing or trading that would treat the grant of security as a trade requiring clearance.

There is no secured financing provision of any kind: no ban, no notification requirement, no disclosure threshold and no minimum shareholding requirement. The loan leg of a funded collar is simply unregulated by this policy.

Absolute ban on buying and selling the same security within 30 days, extending to securities of any close business associate of the Company (joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer). No carve-outs are given for plan securities or for exercise of options, and there is no stated basis (LIFO or otherwise) for matching trades.
rules.evidence: It is also a policy of the Company that employees, consultants and Directors not engage in "short-term" trading in securities in the Company or in any close business associate (such as a joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer etc) of the Company. Short-term trading means buying and selling the same security within 30 days.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chairman (written details of the carrying out of the transaction); Directors must additionally report any change in their holdings to the officer maintaining the Directors' securities register
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 business days of the transaction; Directors' holdings changes within one business day
clearance.section: PROPOSED TRADING; CONFIRMATION OF TRADING; DIRECTOR'S SECURITIES HOLDINGS
clearance.evidence: it is a requirement that any employee, consultant or Director proposing to trade in Company securities first advise the Chairman (in writing) of the details of such proposed trade and not trade until the Chairman advise that such trade is permissible. ... The Chairman will endeavor to respond quickly and, in any event, within 3 business days.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 business days of the transaction; holdings changes within one business day
clearance.evidence: Where an obligation under this policy applies to the Chairman, then any approval or notification that would otherwise be required to be made to the Chairman shall be made to the Managing Director.

short_term.basis: buying and selling the same security within 30 days; no matching basis stated
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading means buying and selling the same security within 30 days.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Managing Director where the applicant is the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: A Person who wishes to seek exemption from this prohibition in order to sell securities during a closed period and who believes that he is subject to exceptional circumstances may seek (in writing) permission from the Chairman to so trade. ... Exceptional circumstances include where the Person wishing to trade is in severe financial hardship.
Also included may be where the Person is required by a court order or enforceable undertakings or some other legal or regulatory requirement to sell the securities.
Trading that the Company may consider excluded from this CP policy includes where the trading results in no change in a beneficial interest in the securities (change of name on register only)

where trading occurs via investment in a scheme or other arrangement where the investment decisions are exercised by a third party , where the Person has no control or influence with respect to trading decisions
and where the trading occurs under an offer to all or most of the securities holders of the Company.

exemption_authority: The Chairman may, on written application, grant written permission for a Person to sell during a closed period where he is of the opinion that exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement) exist, for a specified period of time; the Chairman may also refuse any proposed trade at any time on best-interests grounds. Where the obligation applies to the Chairman himself, the Managing Director stands in his place. Any exemption is subject to the insider trading provisions of the Corporations Act and ASX restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chairman will seek to determine if he believes that the Company is in possession of inside information or that such proposed trade is, for any other reason, not in the best interests of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for the collar legs, and for any later unwind, roll or physical settlement, rests on an unbounded discretion that can be exercised against a hedging or financing structure purely on optics, so no leg of the trade can be assumed to be approvable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is prohibited ... that [a Person] trade in the Company's securities or in any derivatives created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, unwinding or settling the put and call is barred from 2 business days before each quarterly, half-year and full-year results announcement, which given quarterly reporting closes the window four times a year.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges, hedging or short selling.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by the policy, so the bank's constraints come from the Corporations Act, ASX disclosure and any plan rules or employment terms rather than from this document; the absence of any forced-sale clause also means the policy is silent on a lender selling into a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy makes no reference to employee equity plans, unvested securities, performance rights or options issued as remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Nothing in the policy limits a collar to vested shares, but nothing exempts plan securities from the clearance or short-term rules either, so any plan documents must be checked separately for hedging or disposal restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading means buying and selling the same security within 30 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar established and unwound inside 30 days, or one whose legs are opened and closed against each other in that period, risks being characterised as short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed 30 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Such approval would not constitute a representation that such person would not be in breach of the law in so trading, as it is such person's obligation to make such determination.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Chairman clearance gives the bank no comfort that the director is free of inside information, so the bank must obtain its own representations at each of entry, roll and settlement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: each Director shall promptly (within one business day) report to the Company officer maintaining that register the details of any change in such holdings of such Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A change in a Director's holdings caused by physical settlement, share transfer to a security trustee or lender enforcement must be reported within one business day, on top of the Appendix 3Y/3Z regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not engage in "short-term" trading in securities in the Company or in any close business associate (such as a joint venture partner, major supplier, major buyer etc) of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The short-term ban reaches beyond the Company's own securities, so a basket or index hedge containing joint venture partner securities could be caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is expressed to apply to 'employees, consultants and Directors' and to 'Persons'; it does not define associates, spouses, dependants or controlled entities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express extension to family trusts or controlled companies, so the policy's own reach over a collar held through such a vehicle is untested, though the insider trading law and the procuring provisions still apply.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2017 document that is silent on hedging, derivatives generally, margin lending, encumbrances and secured financing. Both derivative legs and the grant of security over the shares would be treated as proposed trades in Company securities requiring prior written notice to the Chairman and his written permission before execution, with written confirmation of the completed transaction back to the Chairman within 3 business days and, for a Director, a holdings report within one business day. The Chairman has an unbounded discretion to refuse any trade that he considers not in the best interests of the Company, so approval of a hedging and financing structure cannot be assumed, and the same clearance is needed for any unwind, roll or settlement. Execution must avoid the closed periods, which run from 2 business days before each quarterly, half-year and full-year results announcement to the announcement itself and expressly extend to derivatives over the Company's securities. Tenor should exceed 30 days to stay clear of the short-term trading ban, and the policy offers the bank no forced-sale protection because it says nothing about lender enforcement in a closed period.
